subject.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence

question: Should a pre-existing active descendant suppress the yield diagnostic, and if so, what evidence proves that descendant is a relevant pending wake rather than unrelated or obsolete work?
rationale: The runtime currently lacks a canonical causal relationship between a yielded turn and arbitrary session descendants; choosing whether any active descendant is sufficient changes user-visible delivery semantics and cannot be inferred safely from the patch alone.

options.title: Require causal wake evidence
options.body: Suppress the diagnostic only for same-turn continuation or a registry-backed pending wake explicitly associated with the yielded session turn.

options.title: Accept any active descendant
options.body: Keep the broad session-wide suppression rule and intentionally accept that unrelated descendant work may hide the warning.

options.title: Defer descendant support
options.body: Remove active-descendant suppression from this PR and handle legitimate prior-turn waits in a separately designed lifecycle change.

recommendation.title: Require causal wake evidence
recommendation.body: Suppress the diagnostic only for same-turn continuation or a registry-backed pending wake explicitly associated with the yielded session turn.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the agent-runtime terminal-resolution boundary makes this the best available owner for defining its continuation semantics.
